name: Off-Highway Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle used off the roads and highways, with a seat or saddle and no more than two wheels on the ground, that isn't registered for highway use, such as an electric dirt bike like a Sur-Ron or Talaria. No limit on power or speed.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle and no more than two wheels on the ground, used off roads and highways; excludes tractors, mopeds and electric bicycles
No limit on motor power or speed
An off-highway vehicle only while it isn't registered and licensed for highway use
Titled with FLHSMV if bought by a Florida resident after July 1, 2002 or ridden on public lands; FLHSMV may issue a title validation decal as proof
On public lands, a rider under 16 must be supervised by an adult and carry a certificate from an approved OHV safety course
On public lands, a rider under 16 must wear a DOT- or Snell-approved helmet, eye protection and over-the-ankle boots
On public lands it needs working brakes, must stay under 96 dBA, and must show a lit headlamp and taillamp from sunset to sunrise
On public lands, carries no more passengers than the manufacturer designed it for
In state forests it's ridden only on designated OHV trails, with a day-use pass
The unpaved-road allowance in §316.2123 covers ATVs, not off-highway motorcycles
